subject: OpenAI Agents API public beta, September 10 2026
central_claim: OpenAI's September 10, 2026 Agents API public beta is a publishable AI engineering topic because official changelog and API documentation support a bounded E2/R1 claim: OpenAI has turned the Codex harness into a managed API runtime with durable sessions, selectable execution environments, sandboxed command/file work, MCP connections, subagents, progress events and usage observability, shifting agent application design from repeated single model calls toward session and environment architecture. The article does not claim independent improvements in model quality, latency or total cost.

selection.reason: The Agents API changes a concrete engineering decision for agent builders: whether to keep orchestrating model calls, tool state, summaries, command execution and recovery in their own application, or use a managed Codex harness with sessions and environments. Official docs provide multiple primary-source pages for behavior and limitations. The conclusion is bounded because no beta API call, sandbox execution, MCP connection or cost measurement was run in this turn.

claims.claim: OpenAI Agents API public beta exposes a managed Codex harness with durable sessions, configurable environments and tool connections, changing agent architecture from repeated single model calls toward session-runtime design rather than proving independent quality or cost gains.

Opened the OpenAI API changelog. The September 10, 2026 entry says Agents API was released in public beta and describes a managed Codex harness with durable sessions, progress streaming, context compaction, recovery, tool/MCP connections and hosted or self-hosted sandboxes.

Opened the Agents API overview. It defines agent, environment, session and events/items, and says OpenAI manages sessions, orchestration, context compaction and recovery while the application provides tools and chooses the execution environment.
Opened the architecture page. It separates harness, environment and application server, and distinguishes no-environment, OpenAI-hosted environment and self-hosted environment patterns.
Opened session documentation. It documents follow-up input to the same session, steering active work, event streams and session setting changes.

Opened hosted sandbox, self-hosted sandbox and security pages. These pages support claims about workspace behavior, network policy, environment key separation, outbound executor connection and credential risk.

Opened MCP connections and observability pages. These support claims about service-origin vs environment-origin MCP connections, stdio MCPs, credentials, live progress, traces, subagent usage and best-effort token accounting.

Reviewed other OpenAI September entries, including GPT-Live 1 general availability, Prompt Cache Diagnostics, image models, API-key governance and GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6 Astra was already published in the 2026-09-10 AI edition, and the Agents API was a distinct unmaterialized runtime release with broader developer architecture impact.
Opened Anthropic release notes and considered September 14 compact-on-demand. It was already selected for 2026-09-16, so it was treated as covered rather than selected again.

Reviewed Gemini changelog and model-card paths. Gemini 3.8 Flash was already covered on 2026-09-13, and no fresher official Gemini release in this pass outranked OpenAI Agents API on novelty and decision utility.

Reviewed official blog, registry and release-note paths for Qwen, DeepSeek and Mistral because registry-first model releases can be material. This pass did not surface a fresher non-duplicate model or API release with stronger public primary-source evidence and engineering decision utility than Agents API.

Opened vLLM v0.29.0 release signals and checked PyTorch release path. vLLM v0.29.0 is a strong infrastructure alternative because Model Runner V2 became default for all models and release artifacts are public, but the 2026-09-01 AI edition already covered vLLM v0.28.0 and the Agents API offered a broader fresh application-architecture change for this slot.

Search results were used only to discover official OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, vLLM and PyTorch source paths. No article fact or selection decision relies on search snippets, X posts or secondary summaries without opened primary-source confirmation.
